mapName: A Learnable Meta World - Stop Signs

metas.name: Australia - NSW-Three holes
metas.note: In New South Wales, especially in Sydney, some stop signs have three big holes making it unique for this region.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/australia for more clues.

metas.name: Cambodia - ឈប់/Stop
metas.note: Stop signs in Cambodia always have the word "Stop" written in Khmer (ឈប់) in addition to the English word.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/cambodia for more clues.

metas.name: Canada - New Brunswick Arrêt/Stop
metas.note: Stop signs in New Brunswick always have the word "Stop" written in France (Arrêt) in addition to the English word.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/canada for more clues.

metas.name: Canada - Québec Arrêt
metas.note: Stop signs in Québec always have the word "Stop" written in France (Arrêt). Beware that "Arrêt" is also written on New Brunswick stop signs!
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/canada for more clues.

metas.name: Costa Rica - Alto
metas.note: Costa Rica, Guatemala, Panama and Mexico are the only countries using the word "Alto" on their stop signs.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/costa-rica for more clues.

metas.name: Guatemala - Alto
metas.note: Guatemala, Panama, Costa Rica and Mexico are the only countries using the word "Alto" on their stop signs.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/guatemala for more clues.

metas.name: Israel - ✋🏻
metas.note: Israel is the only country that uses a symbol on its stop signs, which makes it unique and easily recognizable.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/israel-west-bank for more clues.

metas.name: Malaysia - Berhenti
metas.note: Stop signs in Malaysia always have the word "Stop" written in Malay (Berhenti).
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/malaysia for more clues.

metas.name: Mexico - Alto
metas.note: Mexico, Panama, Costa Rica and Guatemala are the only countries using the word "Alto" on their stop signs.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/mexico for more clues.

metas.name: Panama - Alto
metas.note: Panama, Guatemala, Costa Rica and Mexico are the only countries using the word "Alto" on their stop signs.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/panama for more clues.

metas.name: SA - South America Pare
metas.note: The word "Pare" on stop signs is widely used in all of Latin America excluding Mexico, Panama, Costa Rica and Guatemala. That means you can spot it in Colombia, Ecuador, Bolivia, Peru, Brazil, Paraguay, Argentina, Uruguay, Chile, Puerto Rico and the Dominican Republic.
metas.footer: Check out https://www.plonkit.net/ for more clues.

metas.name: Singapore - White  square
metas.note: The edge of the stop signs in Singapore has a white square outline making it unique.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/singapore for more clues.

metas.name: Thailand - หยุด
metas.note: Stop signs in Thailand always have the word "Stop" written in Thai (หยุด).
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/thailand for more clues.

metas.name: Türkiye - Dur
metas.note: Stop signs in Türkiye always have the word "Stop" written in Turkish (Dur).
